# Makefile skeleton and conventions

Extracted from brokerdesk PR #76 and enforced by `render.sh --check`.

## Skeleton

```make
# Generated by devenv:makefile-gen -- `make` prints the targets.
# Regenerate: /devenv:makefile-gen --apply --force (keeps Makefile.bak).

PORT ?= 8888
PY   := $(if $(wildcard .venv/bin/python),.venv/bin/python,python3)
LOG  := /tmp/web-$(PORT).log

.DEFAULT_GOAL := help
.PHONY: help build run clear clean

help: ## Show this help
	@awk 'BEGIN {FS = ":.*## "} /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+:.*## / {printf "  make %-10s %s\n", $$1, $$2}' $(MAKEFILE_LIST)

build: ## Build
	<delegated command>

run: ## Run
	<delegated command>

clear: ## Remove build/test artifacts (keeps dependencies, secrets, data)
	rm -rf <allowlisted artifacts>

clean: clear ## Same as clear
```

The variable block is emitted only as needed: `PORT` with a server port,
`PY` for a pip/venv Python project, `LOG` with a log path. No trailing
comments on variable lines -- Make keeps the whitespace before `#` in the
value.

## Rules (`render.sh --check` fails on each)

- **`.DEFAULT_GOAL := help`** — bare `make` prints the target list.
- **Help regex is `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+:.*## `.** Without `0-9`, `test-e2e`
  silently drops out of the list (it happened in PR #76).
- **Help comes only from `## ` comments** on the target line. No hand-written
  `echo` list: that is how a target and its help drift apart (MyAvatar's
  Makefile did not even list `help`).
- **`.PHONY` lists exactly the `##`-documented targets.** Every target is
  documented; every documented target is phony.
- **No `$(VAR)` inside a `##` description** — awk does not expand it.
- **GNU Make 3.81 (macOS default).** No `.ONESHELL`, no `$(file ...)`, no
  other 4.x-only function. Each recipe line is its own POSIX `sh`, so
  multi-step logic uses `&&` or `{ ...; }` on one line.
- **No `$(MAKE)` in recipes.** Compose with prerequisites (`run: build
  serve`, `test-all: test test-e2e`); `make -n` executes `$(MAKE)` lines,
  which would break the no-side-effect verification.
- **Aliases are dependencies**: `clean: clear ## Same as clear`.
- **`stop` is port-based** (`fuser $(PORT)/tcp`) or the run script's own
  teardown (`<bash|sh> ./<script> stop|down`); `pkill` / `killall` are
  rejected anywhere in the file.
- **`clear` never names `.env*`, `node_modules`, `.venv`, `.git` or a
  `data` dir** outside a `-prune` clause.

## Variables

User-overridable values use `?=` (`PORT=9000 make run`). Derived values use
`:=`. Sub-app paths are written literally rather than through a variable —
one fewer indirection, and the report names the source file anyway.
